title: Handy's father's ragtime record and the phonograph
summary: Handy recalls a ragtime one-step record his father's band played and learned from, heard when he was six or seven, and the wind-up phonographs of the time.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What was the man's name again that made that record?

I thought about the name of John Thompson. I wish I could think of the name of it. That was way back around 19... ...six or seven. I couldn't think of the name not to save my life, but the number. But it was a ragtime tune or a jazz tune you'd say? It was a ragtime number. Something like at those times, they called them numbers a one step. Dancers, we called them a one step.
And how old would you be when you first heard the record, do you say?
I was around about six, seven years old.
And your father had had the record for a number of years.

I'll tell you the truth. I don't know how long my dad had had that record. I used to hear him play it a lot. He used to play it a lot on Sundays when his band used to come down at a rehearsal. Mm-hmm. And they played that record a lot to learn it. And they learned to play it pretty good too. Yeah, that particular record they learned it pretty good.
But when you say that record was hot music, jazz music, just like they played here in 1920s? Was it on that style? No, no, no, no.
It wasn't on that style at all. What style was it? It was on, just a ragtime style playing music.
Did they sound like they were reading?
Well, I don't know.
You don't remember the record that clearly, I know.
No, and at that time if there's reading, I didn't know anyway. Yeah. I was too young to know, just reading or just playing by air. I'd like to have it now. Just for memories, you know.
Mm-hmm. Maybe we'll run across it. Was it a cylinder or a flat racket?
I always made something like this, you know, something like that.
A round cylinder? Yeah, it was a round. What's it called a cylinder? Yeah, a round racket. Yeah. It wasn't a flat one. It wasn't like this. It was a cup, they call them also.

Yeah, it was round. It wasn't a flat one like they make these days. It was round ones. But it was a good record because I think my daddy had it quite a while and we played it a lot. And when he wasn't there, we was playing it a lot. We had about 10 or 15 records round there. We'd, you know what I mean, just pick them up and play them any of them. Mm-hmm. And, but I think Thompson had about the best band at that time, so we just, just keep playing over and over and over. And just jumping, dancing, hollering, and go play it again. They had this, what do you call those things? A wind up song? Yeah, yeah. Like an Edison. Wind it up and they had big bells on it, sit out there. I forgot what they called, used to call them, phonographs or something like that.
Yeah, that's huh. Grammophones is another name, do I get. Orthophonics they used to call them.
U stuff I forgot what they called, used to call them, phonographs or something like that.
Grammophones is another name, do I get? Orthophonics they used to call them.
Used to call them orthophonics.
